Maya R: heads-up — our quantization run for llm-v3-conv failed during model bring‑up. converter pulled the HF repo but the safetensors shard index looks inconsistent. dropping logs below.
Maya R: ```
2026-03-18 09:12:03,422 ERROR hf_converter.download: expected shard_count=8, index.json lists 8, but found 9 downloaded shards
2026-03-18 09:12:03,423 ERROR safetensors: shard file 00008.safetensors size mismatch (expected 12,345,678 got 0)
2026-03-18 09:12:03,424 ERROR hf_hub: HTTP 401 during retry (token ok earlier)
```
Simon K: did the converter pin a revision when calling hf_hub_download? sounds like a race where the hub republished assets mid-download.
Maya R: no, converter used repo_id and revision=None (defaults to main). The hub returned different manifests between retries. I saw two different index.json digests in the logs.
Arjun S: can you paste the exact command you used to run the converter?
Maya R: `python -m hf_converter --repo zzz/llm-v3 --out redwood-format --quantize=8bit --use-safetensors`
Arjun S: ok. converter currently retries downloads but does not verify index.json checksum after each retry. If auth flaps you can end up mixing shards from two different snapshots.
Liz P: FYI HF's hub sometimes does atomic repack when a new push happens (they rewrite shards/manifest). If you don't pin revision or verify checksums you can get partial sets. Also, huggingface_hub may return 200 for an index and 401 for a blob if token scopes are scoped to certain endpoints.
Maya R: we confirmed CI token rotated during a window (short-lived deploy token). looks like one shard download failed (zero-bytes) and converter kept going. result: quantized model loaded but produced tokenization mismatches and a 3x perplexity regression on eval sets.
Simon K: immediate mitigation: 1) fail fast on any shard size/sha256 mismatch, 2) add revision pinning via etag/commit hash if available, 3) enforce post-download checksum verification. Also log the HF `snapshot_download` etag.
CI-Bot: Deploy job #457: build failed during convert step (exit 1) — see Maya's thread for details.
Liz P: small patch idea — after listing index.json, cache its sha256 and compare to the etag from HF. After each blob download verify blob sha256 matches index. If mismatch, delete all downloaded shards and retry with `revision=latest-commit` pinned.
Maya R: I'll open a PR in ml-tooling that does exactly that + an extra retry with auth refresh before retrying downloads. tagging @Simon K for review.
Simon K: ack, will review. :thumbsup:
Maya R: for tracking — attaching failing run id: run-20260318-llm-v3-quant1. I'll add an eval diff showing the tokenization corruption vs baseline.
Arjun S: thanks. once fixed we should run the full eval suite (LM, QA, and embed drift) before promoting the quantized artifact.
Liz P: one more note — add a small unit test that simulates mixed-index scenario (two index.json versions, interleaved blobs) to avoid regressions.
Maya R: agreed. i'll include that in the PR.
Simon K: also create a short postmortem in /incidents if this ends up affecting customers.
Maya R: will do.
